issues.description: The problem statement instructs students to initialize the stock attribute in the SealSaloon constructor, but elsewhere (and in the solution) the stock attribute is required to be static (static final). Initializing a static field in an instance constructor is incorrect/confusing: a static final field must be initialized at declaration or in a static initializer. This contradiction can confuse students about whether stock should be an instance field initialized in the constructor or a static field shared across all instances, and it may lead to incorrect implementations.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the specification: either (A) require stock to be an instance (non-static) final field and instruct students to initialize it in the constructor, or (B) require stock to be static final and instruct students to initialize it at the point of declaration or in a static initializer. Update the problem text to remove the contradictory instruction about initializing stock in the constructor when stock is required to be static.
